title: Austin's Mayor Vote, Football & Property Taxes
summary:
*   **Celebrating Local Athletics:** The council recognized the undefeated 1968 John H. Reagan High School football team and individual star players for their outstanding season.
*   **Path to Direct Mayoral Election:** An ordinance advanced to its third reading, setting the stage for a public election to amend the city charter and allow citizens to directly elect their Mayor.
*   **Extensive Property Tax Reviews:** Numerous public hearings were held to address property tax appeals, primarily from the Oak Hill-Manchaca area, with the council largely upholding the Board of Equalization's assessed values.

Mayor Akin announced this was a Special Meeting called for the purpose of passing
Resolutions to honor the footbal members of the John H. Reagan High School; for reading
Ordinance 690206-H through its second reading; and to hear
Tax Appeals scheduled for this date.
RESOLUTIONS HONORING FOOTBALL MEMBERS OF
THE JOHN H. REAGAN HIGH SCHOOL
MAYOR AKIN read a resolution prepared for all members of the football squad, each to have
an original with each individual's name inscribed.
Councilman Nichols offered the following resolution and moved its adoption (RESOLUTION)
WHEREAS, the 1968 John H. Reagan High School Football Team has achieved an undefeated and
untied record, and in doing so, has become the undisputed champion of State Class AAAA
Football; and WHEREAS, this is the second consecutive year during which the Reagan Raiders
have achieved this most distinguished position in Texas high school football; and WHEREAS,
team member Gary Brown has caused recognition from over the entire state as well as the
nation to be focused on the City of Austin; and WHEREAS, in recognition of his
extraordinary accomplishment, with esteem for the character, disipline and sportsmanship
displayed, the people of Austin wish to pay rightful tribute to this young man, Now,
Therefore BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AUSTIN:
CITY OF AUSTIN, TEXAS
February 25, 1969
The appreciation and admiration of the City of Austin be publicly expressed to Gary Brown
of the 1968 John H. Reagan High School Football Team, and a copy of this resolution be
presented to the said Gary Brown.

TAX APPEALS
MAYOR AKIN opened the hearings on Tax Appeals from decisions of the Board of Equalization.
On each appeal, the appelant or his representative, presented the case, which was
discussed thoroughly with the Council and at length. The Tax Assessor reviewed maps,
pointed out recent sales in each area that might indicate the fair market value, discussed
topography, land which might come under agricultural exemption, and pointed out all
factors that affect or have bearing on the value of each parcel. In most instances the
Council made trips to the areas to see the properties on the ground. Each of the following
cases was carefully considered by the Council before a decision was reached.
All appeals discussed are in the Oak Hill-Manchaca area except the property appealed by
John J. McKetta.
